qc.label_under_test: the word piece 'aste'/'aster'/'asted' when it is split off a short prefix (t|aster, ro|aster, -w|aste, dism|asted), as against the same or similar words that are a single token (toaster, master, waste)

neighbours.label: the word piece 'aste'/'aster'/'asted' split off a prefix (t|aster, e-w|aste, dist|aste, dism|asted), strong; the same sounds as one whole token (waste, master, board, toaster) are weaker or silent
fire: The wine taster swirled the glass and frowned at the sour finish.
She looked at the greasy plate with obvious distaste.
The town set up a drop-off point for e-waste such as old phones and laptops.
After the storm, the dismasted schooner drifted for three days before rescue.
Critics dismissed him as a poetaster who rhymed without saying anything.
A carved pilaster framed each side of the old bank's doorway.
The garden path was lined with silver-leaved oleaster shrubs.
I was flabbergasted when the tiny dog chased off the bear.
quiet: The wine expert swirled the glass and frowned at the sour finish.
She looked at the greasy plate with obvious disgust.

predictions: Expect most split-piece fire sentences at 0.5-0.8 of max; rarer words like pilaster/oleaster/flabbergasted may be whole tokens or split differently and could miss. Near misses should stay below 0.3.
